# Summary

In assessing compliance with our [Data and Code Availability Policy](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/journals/jpe/datapolicy), our reproducibility team has identified the following issues, which we ask you to address:

1. The README is clearly AI generated. While this is not a problem per se, significant work is needed to make this less verbose and clearer for a human reader. The main purpose here is to get enough documentation so that a replicator can reproduce the results. If there are additional informations, put those in a dedicated section at the end. The exercise where you re-run the LLMs should be somewhere towards the end, as this is not central to the paper results, as we discussed.
2. Can you help us to find working installation instructions for the Rcpp error we found? Probably a missing library our side, but that should be documented.
3. We failed at step 11 because didimputation is not part of the environment. Please add.
4. We got a timeout error, which is weird - there is a 120 seconds limit it seems. The system we are using does not have any time limits, so we are surprised. Any ideas?

# Findings {#sec-findings}

- Failed to generate any figure/table because of the timeout error described above.
- While package/environment errors could be troubleshot, I could not determine why I ran into a timeout error. The code runs on a 24/7 available server, which is supposed to be robust to any kind of auto sleep/suspension. 
- Some packages appear to be missing from the instructions, and some additional instructions on environment setup could help speed up replication. See section above for more details.

## Other Issues

- The missing C library was not mentioned because it is usually available on Linux/macOS machines, and the error happened while running `fda-env/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` which appears to recompile some binaries requiring this lib. The missing R libraries are mentioned in the README, but in a different place from other packages, and without an install script.

## Reason for incomplete reproducibility

- [ ] None.
- [ ] `Discrepancy in output` (either figures or numbers in tables or text differ)
- [ ] `Bugs in code` that were fixable by the replicator (but should be fixed in the final deposit)
- [X] `Code missing`, in particular if it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
  - [ ] `Data preparation code missing` should be checked if the code missing seems to be data preparation code
- [X] `Code not functional` is more severe than a simple bug: it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
- [ ] `Software not available to replicator` may happen for a variety of reasons, but in particular (a) when the software is commercial, and the replicator does not have access to a licensed copy, or (b) the software is open-source, but a specific version required to conduct the reproducibility check is not available.
- [ ] `Insufficient time available to replicator` is applicable when (a) running the code would take weeks or more (b) running the code might take less time if sufficient compute resources were to be brought to bear, but no such resources can be accessed in a timely fashion (c) the replication package is very complex, and following all (manual and scripted) steps would take too long.
- [ ] `Data missing` is marked when data *should* be available, but was erroneously not provided, or is not accessible via the procedures described in the replication package
- [ ] `Data not available` is marked when data requires additional access steps, for instance purchase or application procedure. 
- [ ] `Missing README` is marked if there is no README to guide the replicator, or the README is not in compliance with JPE requirements
